newsitem.title: INDIA: India soybean processing dull on poor arrivals.
newsitem.headline: India soybean processing dull on poor arrivals.

text.p: Indian soybean processing plants are operating at lower capacities, with arrivals trickling to a minimum in the domestic markets, traders said on Tuesday.

"Capacity utilisation is around 20-40 percent in the soybean processing industry and it may further dip as availability of raw material (soybean) is poor," said Dinesh Jadhav, a leading oilmeal broker.
Capacity utilisation a year ago was more than 80 percent, traders said.
Domestic arrivals had fallen to around 2,500 tonnes per day compared to 20,000 tonnes at the same time last year.
Soybean was currently quoted at around 11,800-12,100 rupees per tonne compared to 9,300-9,550 rupees in the central Indian markets, the hub of India's soybean industry, traders said.
Indian exporters had so far signed contracts to export around 1.6 million tonnes of soymeal during 1996/97 (November-October), traders said.
Soymeal exports were currently quoted at $281 per tonne FAS compared to $231 this time last year, they said.
